name: Deduct, record and remit withholding tax on fees, with every parameter configurable
priorityReason: The school acts as collecting agent under law. Getting it wrong is a legal exposure, not an accounting inconvenience.

goal.capability: to deduct the tax that applies to school fees, hold it separately, certify it and remit it
goal.outcome: the school meets its obligation as collecting agent and can show exactly what it took and where it went

dataFields.name: Annual threshold
dataFields.validation: The household's fees for the tax year above which tax applies. An annual household figure, not a per-invoice one (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Fee types counted
dataFields.validation: Which fee types count towards the threshold and are taxed. Not every charge a school raises is a fee for this purpose (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Basis
dataFields.validation: Whether the tax is calculated on the gross fee or on the amount after a concession. The two differ materially (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Tax year

dataFields.name: Effective from

dataFields.name: Fees counted this year

dataFields.validation: Calculated from the approved configuration. Never typed (BR-3).

businessRules.rule: Every parameter is configurable — the rate, the threshold, the fee types counted, the basis and the effective date. The legal position has changed over the years, and a rate written into the software is a rate that will be wrong.
No tax is deducted without an approved configuration in force. A configuration in draft or awaiting approval deducts nothing.
The deduction is calculated from the approved configuration. Nobody types a tax amount.

The threshold is assessed on the household's counted fees across the tax year, not per invoice and not per student. A family with three children reaches it faster than a family with one, and that is the point.
Only the configured fee types count towards the threshold and are taxed. Not every charge a school raises is a fee for this purpose.
Whether the tax is calculated on the gross fee or after a concession is configured, because the two differ materially for a family holding a large reduction.
The amount deducted is held in its own ledger account as money owed onward. It is never school income and never a school expense, because the school is collecting agent rather than the party taxed.
A change to the configuration takes effect from its own date and does not recalculate invoices already issued.
Accounts enter the configuration and the School Admin or Principal approves it. A setting with legal consequence is not one person's decision.
Accounts prepare the statutory return for the period, deposit the amount collected and record the deposit against the holding account, so the balance clears rather than accumulating indefinitely.
Each family is issued a certificate of tax deducted, which the parent needs to claim the amount against their own return. A deduction with no certificate leaves the family out of pocket.
Sales tax is a different mechanism and is not handled here. Tuition is generally not subject to it, and a school charging it on a canteen or a shop does so elsewhere.
Where a household's tax position is corrected — an invoice cancelled or credited after tax was deducted — the deduction is adjusted and the certificate reissued rather than left overstated.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Withholding tax configuration → Enter configuration
basicFlow.userAction: Enters the rate, the annual threshold, which fee types count, whether it is calculated on the gross fee or after a concession, and the effective date.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Validates each parameter and holds the configuration at Draft.

basicFlow.navigation: Withholding tax configuration → Submit for approval
basicFlow.systemResponse: Routes it to the School Admin or Principal. Nothing is deducted in the meantime.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Withholding tax configuration → Approve
basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the parameters and approves the configuration.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval and brings the configuration into force from its effective date.
Tracks fees paid per family across the tax year, since the threshold is an annual household figure rather than a per-invoice one.
Deducts at the approved rate once the household has crossed the threshold, and shows it as its own line on the challan.
Posts the amount to its own holding account as money owed onward, never as income and never as expense.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Household tax position → Issue certificate
basicFlow.userAction: Issues each family their certificate of tax deducted.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Produces the certificate the parent needs to claim the amount against their own return.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Tax return → Prepare return → Record deposit
basicFlow.userAction: Prepares the statutory return, deposits the amount collected and records the deposit.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Clears the holding account by the amount deposited, so the balance does not accumulate indefinitely.

alternateFlows.condition: A household has several children enrolled
alternateFlows.behaviour: Their fees are counted together against the threshold, so a family with three children reaches it faster than a family with one (BR-4).
The tax is calculated on the gross fee or on the amount after the concession, according to the approved configuration, because the two differ materially (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: The rate or threshold changes in law
alternateFlows.navigation: Withholding tax configuration → Create new version
alternateFlows.behaviour: A new version is entered with its own effective date and goes through approval again. Invoices already issued are not recalculated (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept the configuration
alternateFlows.navigation: Withholding tax configuration → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts and nothing is deducted in the meantime, since only an approved configuration is in force (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: An invoice on which tax was deducted is cancelled or credited
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Household tax position → Adjust
alternateFlows.behaviour: The deduction is adjusted and the certificate reissued, rather than the household's position being left overstated (BR-13).
The amount collected in the period is totalled, deposited and recorded, and the holding account clears by that amount (BR-10).

departures.requirement: No rate, threshold or basis is written into the software. Every parameter is configured and approved, because the legal position has changed before and will change again.
Tax collected never touches income or expense. It is a liability from the moment it is deducted until it is deposited.
The household's counted fees are tracked across the whole tax year, and a household's position is calculable at any point in it.
Configurations, deductions, certificates and returns are retained 7 years or the statutory period, whichever is longer.

openQuestions.question: What are the current rate and annual threshold?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and the feature is explicit that they must be confirmed with the school accountant before going live.

openQuestions.question: Which fee types count towards the threshold — tuition only, or admission and others too?
Is the tax calculated on the gross fee or after a concession?
openQuestions.assumption: Configurable, but the school's answer is not specified and the two differ materially.

openQuestions.question: What is the tax year, and does it match the academic session?
openQuestions.assumption: It does not. The tax year is set by the authority and will straddle two sessions.

openQuestions.question: How often must the return be filed and the amount deposited?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and it decides the period the return covers.

openQuestions.question: Where a household crosses the threshold mid-year, is tax due on the fees paid before crossing or only after?
openQuestions.assumption: Only after, as modelled. This is a legal question and must be confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Where siblings attend different branches, is the household assessed across both?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and family codes may span branches.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
